install.usage.text:
Usage: api/scripts/install.sh [options]

Installs or upgrades the Hestia backend (no root needed). Running it again
upgrades; values already set are kept.

Options:
  -y, --yes, --non-interactive
                        ask nothing; values not given are last time's or the defaults
  --username NAME       the login name
  --password-stdin      read the login password from stdin (one line); the
                        environment variable HESTIA_PASSWORD works too. Not
                        given, an existing password is kept
  --port PORT           the API's port (default 4791)
  --cors-origins LIST   the frontends allowed, comma-separated, instead of the
                        defaults; `default` goes back to them (the Hestia app,
                        see --status)
  --state-dir DIR       the state folder (default ${MADERA_HOME:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/madera}/hestia)
  --session-prefix P    the start of this backend's tmux session names
                        (default hestia-). Two backends on one machine each
                        need their own
  --tailscale           let your phone reach this machine over HTTPS with
                        Tailscale (your own tailnet only). On Linux without
                        Tailscale, downloads the official binaries, runs them
                        as a user service (no root) and prints a login link;
                        on macOS, install the Tailscale app first
  --tailscale-https-port PORT
                        the HTTPS port on the tailnet (default 443). Pick
                        another (e.g. 8443) when something else already uses it
  --service-name NAME   the user service's name (default hestia-api; on macOS
                        the LaunchAgent me.maderaojen.NAME). Two backends on
                        one machine each need their own
  --command-name NAME   the command's name in ~/.local/bin (default hestia;
                        lowercase letters, digits and - only). Two backends on
                        one machine each need their own; the commands this
                        backend gives an LLM use it too
  --no-service          no user service (systemd on Linux, launchd on macOS):
                        only build and configure (run it in the foreground
                        instead)
  --no-linger           Linux: don't turn on linger (asked by default, on with
                        --yes): the backend and Tailscale stop when you log
                        out. macOS has none: the service runs while you are
                        logged in at the Mac
  --bundled-node        always use a Node.js of your own (in
                        ~/.local/share/hestia/node), even when the system's is
                        recent enough. Done anyway when the system has none or
                        an old one
  --update-node         update the downloaded Node.js to the newest release of
                        its major version (otherwise a newer one is only
                        mentioned; macOS then asks about folder access again)
  --skip-build          skip npm ci / npm run build (already built)
  --deps-only           only pick a Node.js and install the dependencies
                        (building from source); no settings, no service. The
                        one-line installer uses it to prepare a new version in
                        a staging folder
  --status              only show what is installed and the pairing link;
                        changes nothing
  --uninstall           stop and remove the service and the hestia command;
                        settings and state stay
  --purge               with --uninstall: delete .env and the state folder too
                        (only a state folder marked by the install)
  -h, --help            show this help
